adjudication.evidence: P1 (476–489) shows a sharp drop in N/E/U but no sustained platform or return; residual after subtraction remains noisy without closure. P2 is a single-day spike, not a platform. P3 and P4 overlap (574–615 vs 573–618); original U shows a clear step at ~575 with persistent elevated level until ~618, then a sharp drop—consistent with a *single* temporary offset from ~575 to ~618, not two overlapping ranges. Interior observations (E/U) remain elevated and smooth across 575–618, supporting one genuine platform. No return before 618; the drop at 618 is abrupt and matches the onset magnitude in U (~20 MAD), satisfying temporary offset criteria. P3’s start (573) precedes observable step; P4’s end (615) truncates the return. Thus only one genuine temporary platform exists: 575–618.
